business_scope.primary_industry_name: Polyresin Vacuum Casting and Hand-Painted Limited Edition Statues

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57, ss. 11, 12, 51 (unlimited liability company provisions)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: British Columbia Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Finance
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Form 1) and Notice of Articles (Form 2) under the Business Corporations Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; any number of shares may be issued; no escrow account mandatory.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the initial subscription agreement and the issuance of one (1) Class A common share at a par value of CAD $1.00, fully paid in lawful money, be and hereby is ratified and approved; further RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be and hereby is established at the address set forth in the Notice of Articles, with the Corporate Registry as the official records office; and further RESOLVED, that [Name] be and hereby is appointed President, [Name] be appointed Secretary, and [Name] be appointed Treasurer, each to serve until the next annual meeting or pursuant to the articles of incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Online (BC Companies Online) – Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search via the BC Registry Online NUANS system to ensure the proposed name is not contrary to regulations. Submit a Name Request application online and pay the fee. Reserve the corporate name for 56 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to confusion or prohibited character, file a new Name Request with up to three alternative names.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Submission of Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: British Columbia Registrar of Companies via corporateonline.gov.bc.ca
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 (Incorporation Application) and Form 2 (Notice of Articles) online, ensuring the articles expressly state that the company is an unlimited liability company. Attach the articles and pay the $350 CAD filing fee. Submit the application electronically.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar requests further information to resolve a questionnaire, respond within 15 days; otherwise the application is deemed abandoned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Certificate of Incorporation and Initial Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar electronically issues the Certificate of Incorporation. The directors then record the issuance of shares, issue share certificates, and deliver the statement of share capital to the Registry within 30 days if required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not generated due to a system error, request a re-issue through the Corporate Online helpdesk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Directors and Officers and Registered Office Set-up
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold a first board meeting to appoint the President, Secretary, and Treasurer, adopt a corporate seal (optional), and confirm the registered office address. File any changes to the Notice of Articles with the Registrar within 15 days if the address changes.
required_dossiers: Registered office consent letter (if providing address)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office is not acceptable (e.g., not a physical address), file an updated Form 2 with a corrected address.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and BC Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the ULC with the CRA to obtain a Business Number (BN) and Program Accounts (GST/HST, payroll, import/export). For a BC ULC, also check if provincial sales tax (PST) registration is required for retail sales. Ensure all registrations are completed within 35 days of incorporation to avoid penalties.
required_dossiers: Director and officer legal name and addresses
CRA Form RC1 (Request for a BN account)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA or BC ministry requires additional identification documents, provide copies within 30 days to prevent account cancellation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy and local municipality (e.g., City of Vancouver Planning & Development Department)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business License (under the Community Charter) and Environmental Management Act Waste Discharge Permit (if emissions exceed thresholds)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Registration for low to moderate impact under the Environmental Management Act; a full EIA is not required unless the facility is located near a sensitive ecosystem or emits major volatile organic compounds exceeding emission caps.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: VOC emissions must meet the Canadian Ambient Air Quality Standards; wastewater must comply with municipal sewer use bylaws (pH, metals, organic solvents); resin waste disposal must follow the Recycling Regulation and Hazardous Waste Regulation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the local fire marshal under the BC Fire Code; structural engineering inspection of the workshop floor for load capacity; occupational health and safety clearance from WorkSafeBC confirming compliance with the Workers Compensation Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), federal tax administration for income tax, GST/HST, and Business Number program; British Columbia Ministry of Finance, Consumer Taxation Branch, for BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST). Primary portals: CRA My Business Account and Business Registration Online; BC eTaxBC for PST.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the BC Unlimited Liability Company (ULC) under the British Columbia Business Corporations Act through BC Corporate Online. Step 2: Apply for the federal Business Number (BN) using CRA Business Registration Online or Form RC1; the ULC must provide certified articles of incorporation, registered office information, and an authorized representative with a Canadian address. Step 3: CRA issues a nine-digit BN and relevant program accounts, including RT for GST/HST and RP for payroll where applicable. Step 4: Register separately for BC PST through eTaxBC using the same BN; a PST program account (PD) is established. A foreign-owned ULC is required to register for GST/HST once its worldwide taxable supplies in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters, or in its first calendar quarter, exceed CAD 30,000; voluntary registration is available to claim input tax credits and to zero-rate export sales.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — a BC ULC is eligible to elect pass-through classification under U.S. check-the-box rules for U.S. federal tax purposes; however, the Canadian default classification is Entity_Level_Taxation because the ULC is a separate taxable corporation under the Income Tax Act and the BC Income Tax Act for domestic Canadian tax purposes. No Canadian tax statute treats the ULC as fiscally transparent.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no general check-the-box election for entity classification under federal income tax. A ULC may make certain elections under the Excise Tax Act, including the closely related corporation election under section 156 to treat taxable supplies between qualifying registrants as made for nil consideration, and annual or quarterly filing elections. For U.S. federal purposes, the ULC may file IRS Form 8832 to elect status as a partnership or disregarded entity, but that election has no effect on Canadian taxation. Hybrid mismatch restrictions in Income Tax Act sections 18.4–18.6 limit deductions related to hybrid instruments and hybrid entities; there is no statutory hybrid-mismatch election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) plus British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST); GST is a federal value-added tax at 5%, and BC PST is a retail sales tax at 7%, giving a combined headline rate of 12% on most taxable consumer sales in BC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies in any four consecutive calendar quarters or in the first calendar quarter, after which GST/HST registration is mandatory. BC PST: no fixed economic threshold; registration is required before carrying on PST-taxable selling activity in BC, and non-resident sellers soliciting orders and delivering into BC must register and collect PST regardless of revenue volume.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and British Columbia do not currently impose a real-time fiscal clearance mandate, digital stamping requirement, or mandatory continuous transaction control regime. Electronic invoices are acceptable if they satisfy the information requirements of section 223 of the Excise Tax Act. Certain large GST/HST registrants above CAD 1.5 million in taxable revenues are required to file and remit GST/HST electronically through CRA, using web services/API where applicable. PST returns and remittances are filed electronically through BC eTaxBC. Pan-Canadian Peppol e-invoicing is voluntary and does not constitute fiscal clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A GST/HST registrant may zero-rate an export supply of goods under the Excise Tax Act when the goods are exported directly by the vendor or on behalf of the vendor, or are delivered outside Canada to the non-resident purchaser, and the vendor retains written evidence of export. Services performed wholly outside Canada, services supplied to a non-resident with respect to foreign real property, and certain intellectual-property and cross-border services may also be zero-rated. BC PST does not apply to tangible personal property delivered by the seller or common carrier to a destination outside British Columbia or outside Canada. The zero rate is conditional on documentary proof; without substantive export documentation, CRA will treat the supply as taxable at 5% GST, and BC PST may also apply if the property is used, consumed, or delivered in BC.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA B13A, Canadian Automated Export Declaration (CAED), or ACI eManifest where applicable)
Bill of Lading, air waybill, truck waybill, or other carrier-issued transport document
Original commercial invoice bearing export sale terms and non-resident purchaser address
Packing list identifying the exported resin statues and quantities
Inward Remittance Certificate, bank foreign-exchange advice, or SWIFT credit showing receipt of payment from the non-resident buyer
Export sales contract, purchase order, and any export allowance or permit
Delivery confirmation and destination-country customs entry, if readily available
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA audits export zero-rating strictly and may reassess a supply as taxable within the normal four-year GST/HST assessment period, or indefinitely where misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud is established. Unsupported zero-rating is clawed back with net tax, interest, and penalties. Civil penalties for false statements or omissions under the Excise Tax Act may reach 25% of the tax sought to be evaded, and late or unpaid net tax carries daily compound interest. Criminal tax evasion under section 327 of the Excise Tax Act or section 239 of the Income Tax Act can result in fines of up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment. BC PST authorities may also reassess uncollected tax, impose late-filing penalties and interest, and require security for non-resident registrants.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as the monetary authority and operator of the Lynx high-value payment system; prudential supervision of Schedule I banks by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); AML/ATF transaction monitoring and reporting by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC); derivatives and securities oversight by the Canadian Securities Administrators (CSA), including the British Columbia Securities Commission (BCSC). Canada maintains no dedicated exchange-control agency or central foreign-exchange administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible on both current-account items (goods, services, royalties, interest, dividends) and capital-account items (share capital, shareholder loans, portfolio transfers, M&A). The Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act impose no exchange-control permits, prior approvals, surrender duties, or repatriation gates on cross-border fund movements. Profit-remittance hurdles are exclusively tax and verification based: (i) Part XIII withholding tax at a statutory 25% on dividends paid to non-residents, reduced to 5%-15% under the Canada-US Tax Treaty when the shareholder is a qualifying US corporation; (ii) Part XIV branch tax at a statutory 25% (treaty-reduced to 15%) on after-tax business profits not reinvested in Canada when the ULC has made a subsection 216(1) election under the Income Tax Regulations, thereby being treated as a partnership for Canadian tax purposes; (iii) FINTRAC reporting for international electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more; and (iv) bank-side KYC/AML 'purpose of payment' substantiation. Canada follows an open-account, negative-approval model; the Investment Canada Act applies only to acquisitions of control of a Canadian business above monetary thresholds, not to passive treasury inflows into a newly incorporated ULC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement: there is no mandatory timeline, no forced conversion ratio, and no obligation to repatriate or exchange export receipts. A British Columbia ULC may invoice in CAD, USD, EUR, or CNY and retain export proceeds in domestic or offshore foreign-currency bank accounts at its discretion. The only compliance duties are the PCMLTFA's 'international electronic funds transfer' report to FINTRAC for any single incoming or outgoing EFT of CAD 10,000 or more, plus standard record-keeping for large cash transactions (CAD 10,000+) and currency transaction reports. Export receipts are freely convertible at the commercial spot rate without central-bank intervention.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account + Operating Account (CAD/USD dual-currency DDA)
Operating Account + Global Transaction Banking CAD/USD Clearing Account
Operating Account (strongest Quebec footprint; limited BC branch network)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High as a supplementary collections and payout rail; Low-Medium as a primary treasury rail. Under the Retail Payment Activities Act (SC 2021, c. 23), non-bank payment service providers must register with the Bank of Canada; offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, and Stripe Treasury may lawfully hold funds and execute CAD/USD/CNY transfers without holding a Bank Act banking licence, but they are strictly prohibited from taking deposits in Canada. EMI balances are not covered by the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation, fall outside OSFI prudential supervision, and may trigger CRA, CRS, and FATCA foreign-account reporting. Legal constraint: the ULC must maintain a domestic CDIC-covered operating account at a Schedule I bank as the ultimate treasury sink; EMIs are recommended only for preorder collection (Stripe and PayPal workflow), logistics marketplace payouts, and low-value cross-currency sweeps, with each inter-EMI transfer traceable to a specific trade invoice or fulfilment event.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The PCMLTFA and the banks' published KYC policies require positive identity verification of all directors and all individuals with direct or indirect ownership of 25% or more of the ULC, plus a formal compliance interview for non-resident-owned entities. RBC and TD Canada Trust may permit remote account opening through video-verified identity proofing when the corporate package is notarized by a Canadian notary and certified by Canadian counsel; however, in practice most commercial account managers require at least one physical appearance of a director or authorized signatory at a BC branch before activating the account. A universally accepted alternative is appointment of a BC-resident corporate officer under a limited Power of Attorney for banking matters who attends the in-branch interview, while the foreign ultimate beneficial owner is verified remotely by a Canadian lawyer. The BC Business Corporations Act does not require directors of a private ULC to be resident in Canada, so the physical-presence mandate is driven by bank risk policy, not statute.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO (US LLC chain) with no Canadian nexus and imperfect corporate flow-of-funds documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of the BC ULC incorporation certificate and the Delaware/Wyoming LLC certificate of good standing; the LLC's operating agreement and member register; passport copies of every 25%+ UBO; six months of personal and corporate bank statements from the parent chain; background-check results; a Canadian counsel KYC/AML opinion; and a subordination agreement appointing a BC-resident banking agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Preorder/deposit e-commerce model (Stripe and PayPal) generating a high frequency of low-ticket incoming credits with a 60-120-day future fulfilment gap.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform payout reports and settlement bank statements; chargeback-to-sales ratio documentation (target below 0.5%); order-backlog report with customer addresses; supplier pro-forma invoices and purchase orders for resin, silicone moulds, and casting materials; shipping and customs documentation; Canada Revenue Agency business-number and GST/HST registration; a treasury policy memo demonstrating that deposits are recorded as deferred revenue under ASPE.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound disbursements to Chinese contract manufacturers and non-resident IP holders (royalties and licences).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed manufacturing and supply agreements with Incoterms; documentary letter-of-credit drafts and bills of lading; Chinese customs declarations; the registered IP licence agreement; NR4 and Part XIII withholding records filed with the CRA; a defensive transfer-pricing memorandum applying an OECD-recognized method to validate the royalty rate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound equity capital injections from the US parent mischaracterized by the bank as shareholder debt or as a suspicious EFT.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-minute extracts authorizing the issuance of shares; subscription agreement and share certificates; the ULC share register; the parent's board resolution identifying the transfer as an equity contribution; the SWIFT MT103 advice carrying the 'Equity Capital Contribution' purpose text; the T2 filing (or section 216 partnership-election statement); and a legal memo confirming that no Part XIII withholding applies at contribution.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route via SWIFT MT103 from the US parent bank (interior leg via Fedwire or FedACH) to the ULC's designated CAD/USD account at a Canadian Tier-1 bank, with the payment message carrying the ULC legal name, BC incorporation number, and 'Equity Capital Contribution' purpose text. Settlement enters Canada through the Bank of Canada Lynx high-value payment system for amounts above CAD 25,000 and is credited to the operating account at the bank's day commercial FX rate. Pre-advise the bank's relationship manager with a copy of the MT103, the board resolutions, and the subscription agreement before the first transfer to avoid a FINTRAC suspicious-transaction hold. To preserve equity character, execute a written subscription agreement with no repayment schedule and no contemporaneous payments that could imply a shareholder loan; any related debt instrument must be documented with a formal loan agreement and CRA-compliant interest terms.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements, use SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for amounts under CAD 250,000 and an irrevocable documentary letter of credit issued via SWIFT MT700 (at-sight L/C) for larger purchases from Chinese suppliers; follow-on payments use MT103 referencing the L/C number. CAD domestic funding moves over ACSS/Lynx; USD cross-border payments clear through the bank's New York correspondent; CNY remittances clear via SWIFT or the CIPS network to the PRC bank's clearing branch. Recurring reseller and royalty payments should use a standing MT103 template referencing the commercial contract and evidencing Part XIII withholding or treaty relief. Where the counterparty is in a higher-risk jurisdiction, upload the bill of lading, commercial invoice, and certificate of origin to the bank's compliance portal within 24 hours of the transfer. Consolidate FX conversion at the clearing bank rather than executing multiple currency hops, thereby minimizing spread and FINTRAC cross-currency reporting complexity.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/CNY) executed with a Schedule I Canadian bank or a registered derivatives dealer under the BC Derivatives Act and the CSA OTC derivatives regime; permissible when the ULC documents a genuine commercial exposure from preorder receivables, resin imports, or export sales.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CAD/CNY where onshore deliverability is unavailable; permissible for hedging Chinese supplier payables, subject to the CSA trade-reporting thresholds and the ULC's written hedge policy.
Cross-currency basis swaps (CAD/USD) for matched funding of the 60-120-day preorder production cycle; permissible when used solely to cover simultaneous USD payables and CAD receivables.

FX options (plain-vanilla purchased calls and puts on CAD/USD or CAD/EUR) bought from a Schedule I bank; option-writing is disfavoured because it introduces asymmetric risk and may undermine hedge characterization.

Physical spot conversions at the clearing bank combined with a documented 12-month continuous hedging programme; absent a 'financial institution' designation under subsection 142.2(1) of the Income Tax Act, FX gains and losses retain ordinary business-income character and are not subject to mark-to-market taxation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies (BC Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after the fiscal year end; for a Dec 31 year-end ULC, due by Feb 28 of the following calendar year (BCBCA s. 274)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee CAD 82.50; failure to file for 2 consecutive years exposes the ULC to administrative dissolution; certificates of good standing are withheld until the report is filed; officers and directors may be subject to compliance orders.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return and tax balance remittance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), International and Large Business or local Tax Services Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Return due within 6 months after taxation year end; balance of tax due within 2 months after year end (3 months only for Canadian-Controlled Private Corporations; a US-parent-owned ULC is generally not a CCPC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; daily compounded interest at the prescribed rate on all overdue balances; CRA may register a federal lien and garnishee receivables.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST annual, quarterly, or monthly return and remittance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), GST/HST Programs Directorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filers (taxable supplies up to CAD 1.5M) file within 3 months after fiscal year end; quarterly and monthly filers file within 1 month after the end of the reporting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty 5% of net tax due plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; daily compounded interest on unpaid net tax; CRA may assess third-party liability against directors under the Excise Tax Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) return and remittance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Ministry of Finance, Consumer Taxation Branch
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly or quarterly depending on tax volume; due by the last day of the month following the reporting period (e.g., February 28 for January)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% penalty on the unreported or unremitted tax plus daily compounded arrears interest; chronic default triggers a compliance audit and a mandatory clearance certificate before any business transfer.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T4 Statement of Remuneration Paid and T4 Summary (if the ULC has employees)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Payroll and Corporation Returns Directorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of February of the calendar year following the year in which salary or wages were paid
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Per-slip penalty CAD 25 (minimum CAD 100) for up to 50 slips, escalating to CAD 125 per slip for repeat failures up to CAD 7,500; directors can be assessed for unremitted payroll withholdings held in trust under ITA s. 227.1.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No monetary thresholds apply to a BC private unlimited liability company. The ULC must appoint an auditor at each Annual General Meeting unless, as an eligible private company, all shareholders pass a unanimous resolution waiving the audit (BCBCA s. 207(1)). A single dissenting shareholder or any shareholder requisitioning an audit under s. 210 makes a full audit mandatory. Public companies and regulated licensees cannot waive.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, CPA Canada Handbook Part II) apply to a private BC ULC; IFRS is mandatory only for publicly accountable enterprises or where the US parent requires group-wide IFRS or US GAAP books; the T2 filing is prepared from ASPE-based financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: BCBCA requires every company to maintain a Register of Significant Individuals (RSI) identifying any natural person with direct or indirect control of 25% or more of voting shares or contractual control. On each share transfer, the directors must record the new member in the Register of Members and review the RSI schedule for changes in significant control; the annual confirmation protocol updates the RSI as of the fiscal year end and reconciles it against the shareholder transfer ledger before the annual report is filed. Directors who knowingly fail to maintain or update the register commit an offence with fines up to CAD 10,000, and the Registrar may refuse good-standing certificates until the register is brought current.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Central Securities Register - BCBCA s. 117 (required if more than one class of shares)
Register of Significant Individuals (UBO with 25% or greater control)
Minute Book containing minutes of general meetings and directors' resolutions - BCBCA s. 224
Accounting records sufficient to enable the preparation of financial statements - BCBCA s. 224; ITA s. 230 retention period 7 years

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 475–1,100 (CAD 650–1,500) per year for a BC corporate registered-office and registered-agent arrangement
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 15,000–35,000 if a full statutory audit is requisitioned (CAD 20,000–50,000); USD 0 for any year in which a unanimous audit-exemption waiver is passed by all shareholders

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small business deduction (9% federal + 12% BC on first CAD 500,000 active business income), SR&ED tax credits, accelerated capital cost allowance

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed via CRA's e-file (NETFILE) or paper
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 6 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 year-end due June 30)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income (gross revenue from all sources)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Canadian-source income only; allocate based on treaty if applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductions (business expenses, capital cost allowance, etc.)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim deductions directly related to Canadian-source income; maintain supporting documentation
Apply treaty provisions to reduce taxable income if applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal and provincial tax payable before credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate based on allocation of income to BC if permanent establishment exists

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax credits (e.g., foreign tax credits, investment tax credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim credits for foreign taxes paid on income also taxed in Canada

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of balance owing plus 1% per month for up to 12 months, plus interest on late amounts

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (non-treaty) or reduced under treaty (e.g., 5% for US corporate shareholder with 10% ownership)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: File NR4 and NR7 forms; obtain Certificate of Residence (TRC) from foreign tax authority; submit to CRA for reduced withholding
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25% statutory, 10% under US treaty (0% for some); Interest: 25% statutory, 0% under US treaty (arm's length)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 (total value of transactions with non-residents in a taxation year)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have specific ESR but applies General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and requires economic substance for treaty benefits; transactions must have commercial rationale

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of income, false deductions, or misrepresentation of facts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties up to 200% of tax evaded, fines up to CAD 1,000,000, imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid taxes and penalties if they failed to remit withholdings or knowingly participated in evasion

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Lack of economic substance, no real business operations, or artificial transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment, denial of treaty benefits, penalties up to 50% of tax benefit
